title: Derived Mayer–Vietoris triangle for a two-open cover
statement: Let W be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U and V be quasi-compact open subschemes with W = U union V, and write j_U:U \to W, j_V:V \to W, and j_{UV}:U intersect V \to W for the open immersions. For every E in D_{QCoh}(O_W) [def-pc-derived-category], there is a distinguished triangle E \to R(j_U)_* E|_U direct-sum R(j_V)_* E|_V \to R(j_{UV})_* E|_{U intersect V} \to E[1] in D_{QCoh}(O_W) [def-pc-derived-direct-image], with the quasi-coherence of the derived direct-image terms supplied by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh]; the first map is the pair of restriction adjunction maps and the second map is the difference of the two restriction maps.

source.place: Lemma cohomology-lemma-exact-sequence-j-star, Tag 08BV, distinguished Mayer–Vietoris triangle for a ringed space covered by two open subspaces; specialized here to a qcqs scheme and quasi-coherent derived categories

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution E \to I of a representative complex for E, with every I^n injective, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For each of the open immersions j_U, j_V, and j_{UV}, the termwise restrictions j^{-1}I are K-injective by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open]. By the definition of the derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image], the complexes j_{U*}j_U^{-1}I, j_{V*}j_V^{-1}I, and j_{UV*}j_{UV}^{-1}I represent the three derived direct images in the asserted triangle.

source.place: Tag 08BV proof via a K-injective resolution and Tag 08BS

proof.text: There is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes 0 \to I \to j_{U*}j_U^{-1}I direct-sum j_{V*}j_V^{-1}I \to j_{UV*}j_{UV}^{-1}I \to 0. On sections over an open T of W, the first map is restriction to U and V; its kernel is zero and its image is the equalizer by the sheaf gluing axiom. The last map is the difference of restrictions. Put T_U=T intersect U and T_V=T intersect V. Since I^n is injective, [lem-sc-ringed-space-injective-restriction-surjective] gives a surjection I^n(T_U) direct-sum I^n(T_V) \to I^n(T_U intersect T_V), and T_U intersect T_V=T intersect U intersect V, so the last map is surjective on sections over T. Thus the displayed sequence is exact on every test open T and in every degree.

source.place: Tag 08BV proof, exact sequence 0 -> F -> j_{U*}F|_U + j_{V*}F|_V -> j_{UV*}F|_{U cap V} -> 0

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the preceding degreewise short exact sequence. Its distinguished triangle is I \to j_{U*}j_U^{-1}I direct-sum j_{V*}j_V^{-1}I \to j_{UV*}j_{UV}^{-1}I \to I[1], and the first two arrows are respectively the pair of restriction maps and their difference. Transporting along the quasi-isomorphism E \to I identifies this with the claimed triangle in D(O_W). This uses the non-split short-exact-sequence triangle, not a degreewise-split construction.

source.place: Tag 08BV, derived triangle obtained from the exact sequence of complexes

proof.text: The construction gives a distinguished triangle in the full category D(O_W) for every E. Since U, V, and U intersect V are quasi-compact and the open immersions are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh] places each displayed derived direct image in D_QCoh(O_W); restriction preserves quasi-coherent cohomology by exactness and the affine-local definition. Therefore, when E lies in D_QCoh(O_W), the same triangle is a triangle in D_QCoh(O_W), as stated.
